hooks.text: One bizarre nebula is colder than the Big Bang itself.
At just one Kelvin, the Boomerang Nebula defies physics.
The coldest place in the universe hides inside a dying star.

title: The Coldest Place in the Natural Universe
description: Discover the Boomerang Nebula, a dying star creating temperatures colder than the background glow of the Big Bang.

beats.text: One bizarre nebula is colder than the Big Bang itself.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope image of the Boomerang Nebula, 1998

beats.text: Located five thousand light-years away in Centaurus, this object reaches a bone-chilling one Kelvin.
beats.visual: The constellation Centaurus in the night sky

beats.text: While the afterglow of the Big Bang warms space to two point seven Kelvin, the nebula plunges to minus two hundred seventy-two degrees Celsius.
emphasis: minus two hundred seventy-two degrees Celsius
beats.visual: Map of the Cosmic Microwave Background radiation by Planck satellite

beats.text: Astronomers Keith Taylor and Mike Scarrott named it around nineteen eighty after telescopes revealed a curved, asymmetrical shape.
beats.visual: The Anglo-Australian Telescope at Siding Spring

beats.text: Later Hubble images exposed its true bow-tie form as a young planetary nebula.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope in Earth orbit

beats.text: A dying central star is shedding mass up to one hundred times faster than similar stars.
beats.visual: Artist illustration of a red giant star shedding gas
queries: red giant star shedding layers illustration

beats.text: Blasting gas outward at hundreds of thousands of kilometers per hour causes extreme adiabatic cooling.
beats.visual: The Swedish-ESO Submillimetre Telescope in Chile

beats.text: That rapid expansion drops temperatures below cosmic microwave radiation, explaining why.
beats.visual: Hubble Space Telescope image of the Boomerang Nebula, 1998

better_than_last: This episode strictly incorporates the reviewer's text on Beat 8 while maintaining a grammatically complete final sentence that sets up a perfect loop back to the hook.
